podcast.body: The distinctive opening of Manu Dibango's "Soul Makossa" was famously incorporated by Michael Jackson into his 1982 song "Wanna Be Startin' Somethin'" from the "Thriller" album. "Michael Jackson borrowed that for want to be starting something in 1982."

podcast.body: This 45-single became a pivotal early disco hit in 1972, initially popularized by DJ David Mancuso at his Loft house parties and later by legendary WBLS Radio DJ Frankie Crocker, who gave it heavy radio rotation. Cited by music journalist Vince Aletti as the perfect example of the emerging disco sound, it demonstrated the power of DJs in breaking hits and highlighted the African roots of disco. "In 1972, Manucuso came across the 45 for Soul Macosa and he started playing it at his parties."

podcast.body: The single version of this song successfully entered the Billboard Top 40 in 1973, despite its chart performance being complicated by the proliferation of multiple bootlegged versions. "Soul Macosa's the single snuck into the Billboard top 40 in 1973."
